summary: Full validation of the new CRAZY-dev watch feature + regressions. Backend GET /api/bot/status.dev_watch is wired correctly (configured=true, stake_usd=25 == min_trade_usd, counters present). State transitions verified live: autopilot ON -> state='autopilot'; autopilot OFF with dashboard WS open -> state='watching'; both via /api/autopilot/on and /api/autopilot/off (restored to original OFF). Mongo collection operator_presence has {_id:'dashboard', clients:1, pod:..., ts:...} fresh (~8s old, inside the 15s window). Frontend header renders data-testid='dev-watch-badge' with data-state='watching' and text 'CRAZY WATCH'; title tooltip includes stake, crazy_seen/fired/tagged_open and skipped counters; header layout is intact. Regression: POST /api/scanner/manual-buy/{mint} on a live SOL candidate returned 200 ok (paper), opened an active row (long_term_hold=false, dev_watch=false as expected for non-dev-watch entry), and POST /api/trades/{id}/exit closed it cleanly (0 active after). Pytest suite 'test_dev_watch.py test_manual_hold.py test_reputation.py test_iter30_manual_holds_api.py' passed 34 passed, 3 skipped in 6.42s. GET /api/trades/active returns 200 with no 500s.
critical_code_review_comments: NOTE: The agent-to-agent context note stated 'autopilot was ON' but observed initial state was autopilot_enabled=false (dev_watch.state='watching'). Final state was restored to OFF, matching what was found. If the main agent expected it ON, the operator will need to re-arm via POST /api/autopilot/on.
bot.py (5000+ lines) and server.py (3600+ lines) still exceed the 700-line maintainability threshold flagged in prior iterations — not blocking but recommend module split.

Dev-watch firing path (CRAZY lookup -> operator buy with no gates, long_term_hold+dev_watch markers, operator exits via x) cannot be exercised end-to-end without a live CRAZY launch; pytest already covers via monkeypatched lookup. The status/presence/badge/toast surface area is wired correctly.
